## Task 1: Climbing expeditions

The 2020-09-22 TidyTueday datasets are about climbing expeditions. From the three datasets, use the "expeditions". Reproduce the plot below! Notice a few things:

-   Use `forcats::fct_lump()` to get the 15 most frequent peaks, and drop the "Other" category.
-   The bars are ordered by the sum of all expeditions (use `fct_reorder()`).
-   The bar colors use the viridis palette and light theme.

```{r, message=FALSE}
# 1. Load the dataset
expeditions <- readr::read_csv("C:/Users/BI/Downloads/expeditions.csv")
glimpse(expeditions)

# 2. Keep the 15 most frequent peaks, remove Other, reorder the sum of all expeditions
peak_data <- expeditions %>%
  mutate(peak_name = forcats::fct_lump(peak_name, n = 15)) %>%
  filter(peak_name != "Other") %>%
  count(peak_name, season, name = "total_expeditions") %>%
  group_by(peak_name) %>%
  mutate(peak_total = sum(total_expeditions)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(peak_name = forcats::fct_reorder(peak_name, peak_total))

# 3. Create bar chart
ggplot(peak_data, aes(x = total_expeditions, y = peak_name, fill = season)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_light() +
  labs(x = "Number of expeditions", y = NULL, fill = "season", title = "The 15 most popular peaks stacked by season of expedition") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Task 2: PhDs awarded

The 2019-02-19 TidyTueday dataset is about phd-s awarded by year and field. There is only one dataset, it is called `phd_by_field`. Reproduce the plot below!

Notes:

-   First you have to aggregate the data to count all phd-s by broad fields.
-   To make the x axis breaks pretty, use `scales::pretty_breaks()`, to make the y axis labels comma formatted, use `scales::comma_format()`.
-   The line size is 1.2, the colors are from the brewer "Dark2" palette. The theme is set to minimal.

```{r, message=FALSE}
# 1. Load and inspect dataset
phd_field <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2019/2019-02-19/phd_by_field.csv")
glimpse(phd_field)

# 2. Count all PhDs by broad fields and by year
phd_by_year <- phd_field %>%
  group_by(year, broad_field) %>%
  summarise(total_phds = sum(n_phds, na.rm = TRUE))

# 3. Create line chart
ggplot(phd_by_year, aes(x = year, y = total_phds, color = broad_field, group = broad_field)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = "Broad field", title = "Number of awarded Ph.D.-s in the US by year") +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm")) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format()) 
```
